name: the_registration_pull
conceit: RETIRED AS DESIGNED. The pitch was two independently-generated vellum drawings (a base psalm-page vignette layer and a separate translucent overlay layer) meant to visually register/align into one match at a single point, printmaker-proof style. Across all 3 stills of the concept, the two 'layers' were rendered as ONE composited plate by the model each time -- there was never a real second independently-generated layer to align against, and nano_banana_pro cannot be relied on to produce two separate generations that align pixel-for-pixel with each other on request. Three real attempts (the base-page still, the overlay-settling still, and the close-match-point still, the last needing an nsfw-false-positive retry on top of that) never produced a genuine two-layer registration. Do not attempt to patch this card -- the working replacement mechanic (a code-only split/unify grade on ONE plate, never two independent generations) is a separate new card, the_undivided.

anti: any beat that requires two independently-generated images to align or register with each other -- no diffusion model call can guarantee pixel-for-pixel alignment across two separate generations; use the_undivided's code-only split/unify primitive on ONE plate instead

plate_bill.must_contain: single manuscript page with 3 soft-edged margin vignettes (pierced hands, mocking crowd, folded garment and lots), bare aged vellum center, no legible script
manuscript page seen through an offset translucent vellum overlay carrying its own near-matching vignette, two small registration cross-marks at the corners
extreme close-up on one match point: scattered lots/garment on the lower layer, dice on the upper vellum layer, meant to align precisely, a glowing registration cross-mark at the point of overlap

motion_slots.earned_by: retired -- no motion budget applies; do not animate any of these three stills as this device.

beat_template.hook: the psalm leaf, its own margin vignettes
beat_template.pivot: a second vellum layer settles, meant to register against the first
beat_template.landing: one match point, meant to align precisely -- never actually verified to align

score_shape: n/a -- retired before any score pass was designed against it.
